USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Excessive catharsis

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient taking lactulose for hepatic encephalopathy develops eight watery stools daily, orthostatic dizziness and muscle weakness. Serum potassium is low. Which explanation best links the treatment to these findings?

  1. Selective destruction of renal collecting ducts
  2. Inhibition of intestinal water secretion
  3. Excessive gastrointestinal water and potassium losses
  4. Direct inhibition of aldosterone synthesis
  5. Obligatory potassium uptake into skeletal muscle
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Excessive gastrointestinal water and potassium losses

The regimen needs reassessment; more catharsis is not necessarily better encephalopathy control.

Understanding the options

Excessive gastrointestinal water and potassium losses
The regimen needs reassessment; more catharsis is not necessarily better encephalopathy control.
Direct inhibition of aldosterone synthesis
Lactulose does not primarily act through adrenal steroid synthesis.
Obligatory potassium uptake into skeletal muscle
The clinical setting points to gastrointestinal loss rather than an intracellular shift.
Selective destruction of renal collecting ducts
This is not the usual mechanism of lactulose-associated electrolyte disturbance.
Inhibition of intestinal water secretion
The observed diarrhea indicates increased stool water loss, not suppression of it.
